# Isomorphic Strings

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/isomorphic-strings)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

Given strings `s` and `t`, decide whether they are isomorphic.

Strings are considered isomorphic if each character in `s` can be consistently substituted to obtain `t`, using a one-to-one correspondence and keeping character positions in the same order.

## Examples

Example 1:

Input: `s = "paper", t = "title"`

Output: `true`

Example 2:

Input: `s = "abca", t = "zbxz"`

Output: `true`

## Constraints

* `1 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^4`
* `t.length == s.length`
* Both `s` and `t` contain only valid ASCII characters.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think about mapping each character in s to a character in t, but the mapping must be one-to-one in both directions.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use two hash maps (or arrays) to track the mapping from s to t and from t to s simultaneously.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The tricky edge case is when two different characters in s map to the same character in t, which violates the one-to-one constraint.

</details>
